usage_note: TRAP: 'phở' (pho) needs its tone mark — without it the word changes. Savory noodle soup is a common Vietnamese breakfast, breakfast is not sweet-first here.
TRAP: 'bò' (bo, beef) tone mark is semantic; wrong/absent tone = different word entirely.
'bánh' (banh) = cake or bread depending on compound (banh mi, banh xeo). Accent required.
'cà phê' (ca phe) coffee, often ca phe sua (with condensed milk) at breakfast.
'bữa sáng' = morning meal; savory-first, not a sweet-pancake default.
'yến mạch' oats/oatmeal; the diacritics on both syllables are load-bearing.
Protein commonly kept as the English loanword in Seattle Vietnamese-American register.
'cháo' savory rice porridge, a common Vietnamese breakfast; reinforces savory-first morning, not sweet-pancake default.
'ngon' tasty; food-appeal register that lands in social captions.
'sữa' milk; ca phe sua and cereal-milk contexts. Tone mark semantic.
